items.titleEn: Metals weaken as front-end yields, Hormuz risk offset softer dollar - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were lower and spot silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Tuesday, as traders cut exposure ahead of Wednesday’s U.S. inflation report while front-end Treasury yields and December Federal Reserve rate-hike risk remained firm. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,160.80 an ounce, down 0.24% on the session, while spot silver was trading near $59.090, down 1.82%. North American equities closed slightly lower as bank earnings failed to offset renewed pressure on chip stocks. The S&P 500 fell 1.79 points, or less than 0.1%, to 7,805.45. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 180.45 points, or 0.3%, to 51,670.10. The Nasdaq Composite fell 41.52 points, or 0.2%, to 27,204.38, while the Russell 2000 dropped 11.11 points, or 0.4%, to 2,783.37. European equities also closed mostly lower after a volatile session, with technology weakness offsetting the support from lower oil and easier long-end yields. The Stoxx Europe 600 fell 0.10% to 635.01. France’s CAC 40 lost 0.07% to 7,827.63, Germany’s DAX slipped 0.10% to 25,259.90 and the U.K. FTSE 100 declined 0.06% to 10,650.33. Italy’s FTSE MIB added 0.04% to 50,057.18.

items.titleEn: SpaceX stock falls 4% today: here's why
Silver's industrial demand, mining dynamics and free float mean price rally might not impact supply until it overwhelms it – Sprott's Zhu
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Silver has key differentiators that insulate the impacts of the price action from the underlying supply and demand dynamics – but when investors do pile into silver, the grey metal’s constrained physical supply means the market can go parabolic in a way that gold is unlikely to ever do, according to Kenny Zhu, Director of Research and Investment Strategy at Sprott. In a recent interview with Kitco News, Zhu discussed three factors that cause silver to behave quite differently from gold. First, he said that because 50% to 60% of silver demand comes from industrial applications, silver prices don’t impact supply the same way gold prices impact supply for the yellow metal. “Gold pretty much drives the underlying trend for the whole segment, like it or not,” he said. “But silver, palladium, and platinum, there's a supply-demand factor at play, but there's also the industrial factor. And that's something that gold isn't really impacted by in the direct way that those other metals are.”

Silver prices could be headed back to $50 - Bloomberg's McGlone
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Silver prices could remain under pressure for years as the precious metal struggles to recover from its historic rally, and one market strategist warns that prices could fall back to $50 an ounce in the near term before finding meaningful support. In a recent note, Mike McGlone, senior commodity strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, said that silver faces a difficult technical outlook, with prices potentially remaining trapped between $50 and $84 an ounce for years. The bearish outlook comes as spot silver currently trades at $59.11 an ounce, down nearly 2% on the day.
